dedupe_keys.name: palisades fire 2025 structure level predictors and spatially validated geoai outputs

description: This dataset holds analysis-ready inputs and derived products from a spatially validated GeoAI study of residential structure destruction in the January 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles. It was deposited on Zenodo on 22 August 2026 (version 1.0.0) by Parastoo Farajpoor and Mohammadreza Narimani of the University of California, Davis. The derived-data archive has the study boundary, a structure-level feature table, model diagnostics (out-of-fold predictions and SHAP samples) and figures; the raw archive has clipped Sentinel-2, Landsat, LANDFIRE, terrain and census layers to rebuild predictors. Coverage: 9,883 residential structures, 5,566 of them destroyed; more buildings within 100 m raised and higher vegetation moisture at 100 to 300 m lowered the odds of loss, with spatially cross-validated ROC-AUC of about 0.75. Access: Zenodo (67 MB derived, 298 MB raw) with code on GitHub. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0, with source layers under their own licences; free. Caveats: the authors say the products support association and neighbourhood screening, not parcel-level insurance scores. Simulation uses: calibrating structure-loss models for urban wildfire and testing building-density and defensible-space scenarios. Related records: the Kutupalong camp fire case study and First Street climate risk data.
